glosses.note: “God” goes with en-words (God dag, God kväll); ett-words take “gott”. “Gott!” on its own means “Tasty!”.
Means “thank you”, and after a request also “please”: “En kaffe, tack.”
Swedes say “du” to almost everyone, strangers and bosses included. “Ni” is for several people or, rarely, very formal.
Swedish writes language names with a small letter.
“Mig” is the object form: “Hjälp mig” (help me).
“Är” is the present tense for every person: jag är, du är, det är.
The same for men and women.
“Jag mår illa” means “I feel sick” (nausea); “Jag mår bra” means “I'm well”.
Swedish has two genders: “en” for most words (en kaffe) and “ett” for the rest (ett glas). Learn each noun with its article.
